# Crypto fixtures

`aes.json` contains the AES-128/192/256 ECB and CBC vectors from
[NIST SP 800-38A, Appendix F](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/SP/nistspecialpublication800-38a.pdf).

`wheels/pypdf-6.19.0-py3-none-any.whl` is the unmodified
[PyPI wheel](https://pypi.org/project/pypdf/6.19.0/) used by the offline
integration test. SHA-256:
`7e5d6e730e7dae87d560a2cee218b852f6498c8be61966f3cd02ead971e48d14`.
Its BSD license is included in the wheel. This fixture is only used by tests
and is not embedded in the Go package.

`pdf/*.pdf` are generated by `pdf/generate.py` using native Python,
`pypdf==6.19.0` and `cryptography==50.0.1`. They contain one page with the text
“Hello encrypted PDF” and a Unicode title. Passwords are `user-password` and
`owner-password`; `aes-256-empty.pdf` has an empty user password. These files
test compatibility with an independent AES backend. To regenerate:

```sh
python3 -m venv /tmp/go-pyodide-pdf-fixtures
/tmp/go-pyodide-pdf-fixtures/bin/python -m pip install cryptography==50.0.1 testdata/wheels/pypdf-6.19.0-py3-none-any.whl
/tmp/go-pyodide-pdf-fixtures/bin/python testdata/pdf/generate.py
```

`pdf/check.py` runs inside WASI during `TestEncryptedPDF`. It reads the native
fixtures, creates and decrypts new encrypted PDFs, checks user/owner/wrong
passwords, tests Unicode and empty passwords, and exercises padding errors.
Set `PDF_OUTPUT_DIR` to a writable guest mount to save newly encrypted PDFs
for validation with a native reader.
